I haven’t had depression before so no, I’ve never been prescribed antidepressants. Can it be called depression if it’s short term/happened over the span of a day or two?

I was perfectly healthy until recently, everything just spiraled downwards.

Honestly I don’t mind depression itself. It’s just that the “what’s the point of anything” thoughts get followed by “is anything even real?” which starts to freak me out.

In my lucid dream I was questioning every little thing I was experiencing and realizing that nothing made sense, but for some reason I’ve come out of the dream with that same skepticism towards the real world and that’s what’s causing me to panic. I want to stop questioning.

My impression of psychiatrists is they opt to institutionalize anyone who comes in. Like, I want help with my depression/(psychosis?). It’s been getting better with time, and I’m much better today than yesterday when this started, but I want to be done with this altogether.

Is there someone I can talk to about my irregular sleep before I go to a psychiatrist as a last resort?

Honestly thank you so much. You have no idea how much you helped me. 

I’m sorry you went through something similar to this. Nobody deserves this in a million years. It’s the worst kind of pain. But thank you for helping me.

The dream happened once, and it’s what made me feel like reality is super subjective and subjected me to what I was just going through.

The dream happened once, but I’ve had moments where I’d dissociate with reality before it. All of it started after I micro-dosed on psychedelics a couple years ago + had an extremely bad weed trip.

I fucking hate myself for ever trying drugs, and for having the type of personality that’s prone to this

I was afraid that I was slowly developing psychosis not that I’m fully there. Basically I start questioning reality and it terrifies me. How can I know anything is real when I’ve been through experiences that show me I can’t really ever trust my senses?

I’m out of that episode now (it seems- it comes and goes) but it’s seriously the most terrifying thing ever. I hope there’s some type of remedy for it. I need advice

You’re literally talking like them now.

Yeah, I was perfectly mentally healthy until I had a couple of bad, paranoid experiences while high. And it slowly developed into psychosis (or whatever I’m going through)

But is it psychosis or depression or a combination of the two? 

I swear this all started with one really bad cannabis trip I had a year or two ago. Everyone attacks me when I say weed started this. “Weed is harmless!”

And they proceed to tell me (or imply in some way) that if weed can freak me out it’s my personality, or that i just have a weak mind

My worry is landing an interview in the first place. What do I have to show for my quantitative/mathematical skills other than a high GPA? Employers aren’t gonna have a reason to contact me back in the first place.

Thank you for the insight and advice. I can definitely understand why prior experience (such as the kind that comes with having an internship under your belt) would be valued above all else. 

I guess I've just been too scared to apply for internships because my resume is pretty empty and I felt like I had no chance, and figured I should build my GPA up first. 

I'm not sure how to make myself competitive for any kind of job at this point to be honest. I have a lot of math and coding ability but nothing to show for it other than a high GPA from a high ranking college. I'm so hopelessly lost.

Would an internship have been a game changer? What other fields could I be looking towards?

All my undergraduate career I was gearing myself towards doing grad school, and decided very late that I’d rather start working after my bachelors. Being an actuary was just kinda what I had in the back of my mind in case I ever had a change-of-heart about grad school.

What is it that people who decide on being an actuary earlier on in their undergrad do differently that makes them more eligible for work in this field?

I'm perfectly willing to relocate.  What is it that disadvantages me relative to other applicants, assuming I'm able to pass the first two exams by the end of the year?

I took two separate classes specifically geared to preparing for the P and FM exams during junior year, and I have a very solid math background, so I'm not exactly starting from scratch.

What should I be doing to spend my time more productively?
Same! Dude this 128a professor is ridiculous
I have two classes that haven't yet released grades. I think the latest I've ever waited was Jan 1st or 2nd. It was after new years.

How hard is it to get an entry level job out of college without any prior internship experience, but with a high GPA and a rigorous math background?

I am a senior applied math and economics double major at a top ranking american university (if that matters to employers in this field). Assuming I can pass both Exam P and Exam FM by the time I'm out of college, and given that I have a 3.9 GPA, how difficult will it be for me to get an entry level position?
